title: Optional open, indexed `kind` for read-routing (NOT an enum, NOT a retention taxonomy)

epic.name: Coordination Bus v2 (re-scoped): Repo Coordination Bus

story.as_a: coding agent (or the discovery read) that must treat a handoff differently from a status ping
story.i_want_to: tag a channel post with an optional freeform `kind` that is indexed for querying
story.so_that: the bus can route reads by message class (handoff/status/question/...) instead of scanning free-text `key` prefixes that don't hold at platform volume

rationale: The panel's central thesis: the 'no message kind' decision conflated the genuinely-unused RETENTION-TIER taxonomy with the genuinely-NEEDED read-routing/addressing concern — and the tell is that the proposals keep smuggling type back in as load-bearing `key`-prefix strings (`claim:`, `handoff:`, `build-complete-`). A `LIKE 'handoff:%'` scan over the free-text `key` column is O(n) and unindexed at fleet volume. An optional, OPEN, indexed `kind text NULL` gives discovery (40.C1), claim surfacing, and future filtering coherently. It is explicitly NOT an enum (the fleet audit killed the closed taxonomy) and NOT tied to retention (retention stays a uniform 30 days, coordination.ex:35).

background.reference: panel agreed-gap #7 ('Optional OPEN kind is needed for read-routing'); the retirement of the retention taxonomy documented in channel_post.ex:11-19 moduledoc and coordination.ex:33-35.
background.includes: A nullable, freeform, length-bounded `kind` column + a partial index, cast in create_changeset, scanned/bounded like other text, surfaced in the read + MCP.

This story reintroduces ONLY (b), scoped to a routing label with NO enum and NO per-kind retention. Un-bundling a locked OWNER decision on panel authority is a reinterpretation only the owner can authorize.

acceptance_criteria.description: Add `kind text NULL` to channel_posts (migration) and `field :kind, :string` to the schema (channel_post.ex:75-93). It is cast in create_changeset (added to the cast list at channel_post.ex:128), length-bounded (e.g. <=64 bytes, via validate_length count: :bytes like key), blank-normalized to nil (added to normalize_blank list, channel_post.ex:129), and NUL/secret-scanned (added to @scanned_text_fields, channel_post.ex:57). It is FREEFORM — no enum/inclusion validation.

A partial index `WHERE kind IS NOT NULL` supports read-routing: `(tenant_id, project_id, kind, inserted_at DESC, seq DESC)` so a kind-filtered recency read is index-served, not a scan. `kind` is NEVER part of the slot-uniqueness key (channel_posts_session_key_uidx stays exactly as hardened at 20260718000000:22-25) — it is a routing label, not an identity component.

recent_page/3 (coordination.ex:453-472) accepts an optional `:kind` filter that, when present, adds `WHERE kind = ^kind` to the query; absent, behavior is exactly US-39.3 (all kinds). The read response (channel_post_json/1, channel_post_controller.ex:261-273) includes `kind`, and the MCP channel_post/channel_recent tools (index.js ~440-473, ~2266-2320) accept/return it. `kind` is server-stored verbatim from the caller (it is a routing hint, NOT authorization — like host/session_id it is advisory).

Backward compatible: existing rows have kind = NULL and are unaffected; a post without a kind is still a valid append/slot exactly as before. No retention change — expires_at stays now+30d (coordination.ex:556-558) regardless of kind.

SERVER-ENFORCED handoff key (closes the keyless-handoff exactly-once hole): a post with `kind = 'handoff'` MUST carry a non-null `key`. create_changeset validates this (a validate-required-style rule: when kind == "handoff", key IS NOT NULL/non-blank, else a 422 changeset error) so a raw-API caller CANNOT create a keyless handoff. This is load-bearing for exactly-once discovery: 40.C1's exclusion join is `claims.ref = posts.key` and 40.B1 claims by `ref`, so a keyless handoff (key NULL) would never join any claim and would stay visible in directed_handoffs even after being claimed/done — two agents pick it up. The stable `handoff:<anchor>` key CONVENTION (40.B2) is a claude-config /handoff-skill concern (out of scope for this epic), so it cannot be the guarantee; the server-side non-null-key rule is what makes the join enforceable against an adversarial or non-skill caller. (The server requires a key to EXIST for kind=handoff; it does not mandate the `handoff:<anchor>` FORMAT — that stays the client convention.)

test_cases.name: post with a kind is stored and returned
expected_results: the row carries kind=handoff; the read returns it

test_cases.name: kind filter narrows the read
preconditions: posts with kind=handoff and kind=status and kind=NULL

test_cases.name: kind does not affect the slot key
preconditions: a session with a keyed slot post kind=status
steps: same session re-posts same key with kind=handoff
expected_results: it UPSERTS the same slot (kind is not part of uniqueness); body/refs/kind refreshed

test_cases.name: kind=handoff without a key is rejected server-side
expected_results: 422 changeset error (key required for kind=handoff); no row persisted

test_cases.name: kind=handoff with a key is accepted
expected_results: 201 — the handoff carries a non-null key, so a later claim can hide it from directed_handoffs

technical_notes: Migration: `alter table(:channel_posts) do add :kind, :text, null: true end` + `create index(:channel_posts, [:tenant_id, :project_id, :kind, "inserted_at DESC", "seq DESC"], where: "kind IS NOT NULL", name: :channel_posts_kind_idx)`.

Schema: field :kind, :string; add to cast (channel_post.ex:128), normalize_blank (:129), @scanned_text_fields (:57), and a validate_length(:kind, max: 64, count: :bytes). No inclusion/enum check — OPEN by design (panel).

recent_page/3: thread a `:kind` opt; add `|> maybe_filter_kind(kind)` next to the tenant/project/expiry filters (coordination.ex:459-464). Slot-upsert interaction: `kind` does NOT join the conflict_target (insert_opts/1, coordination.ex:355-365) — it is a routing label, not part of slot identity. BUT it MUST be added to the on_conflict REPLACE set (insert_opts/1 at coordination.ex:359, currently `{:replace, [:body, :refs, :updated_at, :expires_at]}` → add `:kind`) so a same-session re-post of a keyed slot with a changed kind refreshes it (TC-40.A4.5). Excluded from identity, refreshed on update.
MCP: add optional kind to channel_post + a kind filter to channel_recent in mcp-server/index.js.
Do AFTER the claim table (40.B1) per sequencing (step 6) so discovery (40.C1) can compose kind + addressing + NOT-EXISTS-open-claim in one shot.

AC-40.A4.5 (kind=handoff requires a key): add the rule in create_changeset (channel_post.ex) — e.g. after casting kind/key, `validate_change(:kind, ...)` or a cross-field check that when get_field(:kind) == "handoff" and blank?(get_field(:key)) → add_error(:key, "is required for kind=handoff"). This is a SERVER validation, not a client convention: the exactly-once discovery join (40.C1 `claims.ref = posts.key`) is only sound if every kind=handoff row has a key, and the `handoff:<anchor>` FORMAT lives in the out-of-scope claude-config /handoff skill. The server enforces key PRESENCE for handoffs; format stays advisory. Add a slot-key note: key remains part of the hardened 5-column slot uniqueness (unchanged), this rule only forbids a NULL key when kind=handoff.
